name: Situla
description: A star 66 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 111710: radius 10.134 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 43.36 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 111710: effective temperature 4656 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.099)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.55 from 2008A&A...484L..21M; the 6 published values span log g 2.5 to 2.71, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 111710: distance 65.574 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.014), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 66 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 43 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,656 K, so 10.134 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 111710: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Kappa Aquarii
quotes.card: Kappa Aquarii is a candidate binary star in the equatorial constellation of Aquarius.
quotes.introduction: Its identifier is a Bayer designation that is Latinized from κ Aquarii, and abbreviated Kappa Aqr or κ Aqr, respectively.
